mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises the cost of capital and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand, which depresses corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when labor market is strong.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces wage growth and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during periods of strong GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of rising consumer confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.2% in the same month signals a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls > -0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed when credit spreads widen substantially.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a precautionary savings regime, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises and GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of rising household confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.4 percentage points for five consecutive months, combined with a decline in average hourly earnings growth (implied by UNRATE and PAYEMS dynamics), signals deteriorating labor cost conditions that compress profit margins and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.4pp for 5 consecutive months and PAYEMS growth slows
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 900K units for six consecutive months signals a prolonged housing market downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong mortgage credit expansion.
